integrity: The full primary text was inspected through the definition of the lower resolvent exponent, Theorem 1.2, the power-weight examples, the real-coefficient equivalence, the dual reverse inequality, and the endpoint questions. The exact power law is proved from the reverse-Hölder characterization of |x|^beta and the local-finiteness clause, with symbolic algebra replayed from the packaged artifact.
scientific_limitations: The exact critical-exponent formula uses the real-coefficient equivalence and is not asserted for complex coefficients. The Riesz-transform interval is the strong range furnished by the source theorem, not a claimed necessity range. Endpoint weak type remains open where the source leaves it open, and the reverse-inequality interval is a proved sufficient range rather than a maximality statement.
title: Exact power-weight critical exponent for real degenerate parabolic Riesz theory
